primary_claim: A gradient-based method that computes the 'refusal gradient' of early-layer SAE latents with respect to the downstream refusal-direction metric identifies interpretable, prompt-relevant SAE features (e.g. a 'sexual content' feature for a hugging-related prompt, an 'infectious disease' feature for a wet-lab prompt) that are causally upstream of refusal in Gemma-2-2b-it, and steering by these individual upstream latents induces refusal responses that are semantically aligned with the specific concept represented by that latent.
contradicts_or_qualifies: Extends Arditi et al. (2024, arXiv:2406.11717)'s three-stage refusal-mediation picture by investigating step 1 (how the refusal signal is computed from the input prompt), which their work left unexplained
stated_future_work: Scale feature discovery beyond individual prompts to generalize across a broader range of input scenarios
Identify causal latents using prompts that already elicit refusal behavior, testing the hypothesis that the refusal metric would already be saturated there
Study latents with low interpretability (e.g. Latent 2213) to understand why they have a high gradient and potentially back-engineer prompts where the model refuses seemingly harmless concepts
Explore systematic methods to determine the most informative early layer to analyze, rather than an arbitrary choice
limitations_stated: Layer selection (layer 5) was unprincipled and chosen arbitrarily
Prompts used were hand-crafted, not representative of randomly selected prompts
Gradients were summed across all token positions within prompts, which may obscure token-specific contributions
quote: This simple approach discovers interpretable features that are both causally upstream of refusal and contextually relevant to the input prompt.
